title: Desktop context menu steals relative mouse position from widget config windows
line: With the desktop or widget context menu open, moving the pointer over a settings window no longer highlights or opens items in the menu.
explanation: While a popup is open, Qt forwards pointer events that reach any other window of the app to the popup, mapped by global position (QWindowPrivate::forwardToPopup). On Wayland other toplevels' global positions are unknown, so an event in the Desktop Folder Settings window was mapped as if that window sat at the screen's top-left, and the desktop QMenu highlighted, opened submenus for and reacted to the item at the window-local position. The real fix is in Qt (patch ready in upstream/ for Qt 6.13); until then the change installs a small event filter while the containment/applet context menu is open on Wayland: it ignores pointer events reaching the menu while the pointer is in an unrelated window and closes the menu on a press there, letting the press reach that window. The workaround is compiled only for Qt older than 6.13.

commits.message:
containmentitem: keep other windows from driving the menu on Wayland

Qt forwards pointer events from other windows to the open menu by global
position, unknown on Wayland, so hovering a settings window highlighted
menu items; before Qt 6.13, drop those events and close it on a press.

BUG: 504809

media.caption: Master: desktop menu open at the top-left, pointer in the settings window's sidebar (520,481); the menu's Icons item is highlighted and its submenu opens
Fixed, same steps: the menu is untouched and the window's own sidebar gets the hover
Master: pointer at (520,515) in the window highlights the menu's Enter Edit Mode
Fixed: same pointer position, no menu item highlighted
Fixed: hovering the menu itself still highlights items and opens nested submenus (Icons > Icon Size)
Fixed: clicking in the settings window closes the menu and the click reaches the window (Icons page opened)

review.text: The diagnosis of Qt Wayland's QWindowPrivate::forwardToPopup forwarding events from unrelated windows with unknown global positions is accurate, and an interim libplasma event filter for desktop and widget context menus is a reasonable workaround while upstream Qt is fixed. However, the patch cannot be merged with a literal QTBUG-NNNNNN placeholder and an unverified QT_VERSION < 6.13.0 guard claiming it is already fixed in Qt 6.13, and ForeignPointerFilter has cleanup and scoping rough edges.
changes: File the upstream Qt bug first and replace the literal QTBUG-NNNNNN placeholder with the real bug number; do not compile out the workaround at QT_VERSION_CHECK(6, 13, 0) until an upstream fix is actually merged in a specific Qt release (otherwise Qt 6.13 will silently regress if the patch lands later or differently).

In ForeignPointerFilter, call qApp->removeEventFilter(this) immediately on QMenu::aboutToHide (before deleteLater()) so reopening m_contextMenu before the next event-loop iteration does not leave a stale filter active alongside the new one.
Scope the intercepted Qt::Popup check to m_menu and its transient submenu chain rather than matching any arbitrary Qt::Popup window in the application.
